observations: A single solar panel with a dark brown, octagonal cell pattern.
The panel is framed in black aluminum.
The glass surface appears clean and free of cracks or heavy scratches.
A watermark 'DON KACHI SOLAR ENERGY' is visible across the center.
The panel is leaning against a wall or other panels in what appears to be a warehouse or shop.
No brand name, model number, or technical specification plate is visible in the photos.

risks.risk: The panel may be a low-quality or counterfeit unit.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the manufacturer's specification label (usually on the back or side).

risks.risk: The panel may be non-functional or have significantly reduced output.
risks.proof: A video showing a multimeter reading the Open Circuit Voltage (Voc) and Short Circuit Current (Isc) in direct sunlight.

risks.risk: The panel may have micro-cracks or hot spots that are not visible to the eye.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the glass surface under direct sunlight to check for 'hot spots' (bright spots).

proof_requests: Photo of the specification label on the back of the panel.
Video of a multimeter test showing the panel's voltage and current output.
Close-up photo of the glass surface to check for hot spots.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
